title: Upstream analysis, runtime and source maintenance
summary: Review ten material upstream changes across reconstruction fidelity, executable analysis, original retro tooling, emulation and maintained native source.
notes: The CPU audit queue contained zero unresolved source or target CPU areas, so the requested CPU lane had no queued decisions to resolve. No architecture or minimum hardware value was inferred. Ten primary commit groups were reviewed, including multi-project boundaries in Firestaff, PHOONZANG, PiST, Amiga Disk Engine and amiga-re-kit; none warranted a separate nested project. The tracker did not compile or execute upstream software.

project.status: Starglider 2 remains byte-exact across 412,736 bytes; six connected disk/media helpers and two shared service-state fields now have bounded roles, while physical-media behavior and minimum Amiga requirements remain open.

identity.narrative: M68k Reversing Toolkit remains the same generated Amiga analysis and reconstruction framework; the reviewed disk/media pass advances the existing Starglider 2 target.

classification.narrative: This remains bounded reconstruction/tooling work: names and fields are admitted from native accesses and control flow without promoting unresolved gaps or physical-media semantics.

source_cpu.narrative: The tracked Starglider 2 input remains Motorola 68000 code; no new architecture is inferred from the analysis implementation.

target_cpu.narrative: The retained output is native Motorola 68000 assembly, verified upstream against the original binary through the existing C/vasm route.

build.narrative: The pass names six existing disk/media helpers, identifies an 80-cycle WORD field and a 5,632-byte alternate-playback countdown, and retains byte-exact C/vasm output with 57 assets and 14 headers.
build.limitations: The tracker did not regenerate the output. Upstream did not repeat unchanged framework tests and makes no new runtime, media-validity, physical-timing or playback claim.
build.next_action: Continue resolving bounded service-state and ownership gaps without converting exact generation into a complete behavioral claim.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed pass adds no minimum Amiga CPU, RAM, chipset or ROM evidence.
runtime_profiles.next_action: Add a runtime profile only after primary documentation or qualified hardware/emulator testing states a concrete minimum.

ai.narrative: Existing explicit Claude contribution evidence remains valid; the reviewed commit does not add a new attribution category.

relationships.narrative: The current restoration remains within the Starglider 2 target and does not resolve the wider predecessor, successor or credited-source graph.
relationships.next_action: Revisit project relationships after the bounded restoration stabilizes.

project.status: Wizardry VII reconstruction adds named maze/region routines and derives typed data-file layouts from C declarations and recovered records; the pinned README still reports 271 of 1,099 routines in C (24.7%).
techniques: semantic C replacement under assembly comparison

identity.narrative: PHOONZANG remains the staged Wizardry VII C/assembly reconstruction and its supporting disassembler/decompiler rather than a new standalone data-layout project.

classification.narrative: The changes extend semantic routine recovery and generate data-file layouts from the declarations and recovered record evidence used by the existing reconstruction.

build.narrative: Upstream adds named maze/region routines plus declaration-driven data-layout tooling while retaining the Manx Aztec/NASM comparison workflow. The pinned README remains at 271 of 1,099 routines in C (24.7%).
build.limitations: The tracker did not run DOSBox, rebuild DSAVANT or reproduce byte comparisons; the unchanged percentage must not be inflated from the number of labels in a commit message.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed commits and pinned README provide no verified minimum CPU, RAM or DOS configuration beyond the existing build dependencies.

ai.narrative: README explicitly integrates a Claude reversing agent; source judgments remain bounded by actual inspected routines.

relationships.narrative: Repository also contains disassembler/debugger tooling, but substantial named Wizardry VII recovery earns a subject entry.

project.status: Firestaff now hash-locks four authentic DM1 SNES cartridge images, decodes both H03 ROMDUNGEON slots and validates their shared 14-map structure; native SNES runtime, rendering, input and audio remain out of scope.

identity.narrative: Firestaff remains the clean-room Dungeon Master-family engine and evidence framework; the SNES work is another bounded original-media path inside the same project.

classification.narrative: The new SNES decoder is authenticated-media analysis supporting a clean-room reconstruction, not proof of a complete SNES port or campaign implementation.

source_cpu.narrative: Existing x86, m68k, HuC6280, SH-2 and 65C816 source-family decisions remain supported by the documented original-platform scope; no new CPU is established by this pass.

target_cpu.narrative: Published v3.0.416 assets retain x86-64 and arm64 modern outputs. Asset publication is not converted into an unstated minimum CPU generation.

build.narrative: A skip-safe real-media test hash-locks four local SMC images, decodes both H03 ROMDUNGEON slots and verifies the shared 14-map dungeon structure without tracking ROM bytes.
build.limitations: Cartridge admission, remaining resource readers, tile/palette mapping, controller input, SPC/music handling and version-specific behavior gates remain before any native SNES runtime claim.
build.next_action: Continue from authenticated SNES media classification into bounded resource readers without claiming a native runtime before rendering, input and audio gates exist.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Existing evidenced Mac mini M4 and QEMU-hosted Linux x86-64 profiles remain valid. v3.0.416 publishes additional assets but does not establish a new measured minimum CPU, RAM or OS floor.

ai.narrative: Existing explicit Claude contribution evidence remains scoped to evidenced commits; the reviewed release metadata does not justify broadening the project-level claim.

relationships.narrative: SNES DM1 is retained as a platform variant within Firestaff's shared Dungeon Master-family scope, not split into a second catalogue project.

project.status: ND500X documents and indexes the ND-5000 '87 extension: 23 of 25 manual-labelled instructions are represented, with explicit implementation plans and unresolved RHOLE/AMODB scope.

identity.narrative: ND500X remains the C11 Norsk Data ND-500-family CPU emulator; the '87 material extends its existing ND-5000 instruction scope.

classification.narrative: This is emulator and software-archaeology work grounded in the ND-500 reference manual, with documentation and implementation state kept distinct.

source_cpu.narrative: Documented source/input platforms: Norsk Data ND-500. Processor scope: ND-500.

target_cpu.narrative: No fixed target CPU is established; portability of the implementation language is not proof of supported architectures.

build.narrative: The generated extension page counts 23 of 25 manual-labelled '87 instructions in instructions.json, adds extension tagging and opcode-matrix filtering, and keeps RHOLE/AMODB explicitly absent. The follow-up plan distinguishes existing emulator behavior from unimplemented semantics.
build.limitations: The tracker did not compile or execute the emulator; documentation coverage is not treated as instruction-semantic correctness or hardware validation.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed extension documentation states no verified host CPU, RAM or OS minimum and does not identify a new runnable hardware profile.

ai.narrative: No explicit actual development-AI attribution found in bounded README, implementation front matter and latest commit-message inspection. Unknown rather than non-use.

relationships.narrative: Sibling ND100X uses ND500X as a library/submodule for ND-5000 attached-CPU support; each repository provides a different CPU implementation.

project.status: Castlevania Symphony of the Night decompilation has begun RBO6 boss-overlay asset/entity recovery and corrected Saturn stage-15 sprite/table typing; broader PC and overlay coverage remains incomplete.

identity.narrative: The repository remains the multi-version Symphony of the Night decompilation; RBO6 and Saturn stage-15 work are bounded overlays within the same project.

classification.narrative: The reviewed changes are matching decompilation and data extraction/typing work, not a complete modern-source port.

build.narrative: RBO6 now has its initial assets and common entity data, including one function unified across US and PSP versions. Saturn stage 15 receives corrected sprite splitting and typed water, breakable and gold tables.
build.limitations: Upstream describes the RBO6 work as an initial step with no single large completeness change; the tracker did not build any version or verify matching output.

runtime_profiles.narrative: These overlay and typing commits state no new minimum hardware or verified native-PC runtime configuration.

ai.narrative: No explicit completed-work AI disclosure established in inspected evidence. Config files, workflow instructions and algorithmic neural features alone are not proof of authorship.

relationships.narrative: Screened URL, title and prior decisions. GitHub fork flag is not treated as conclusive lineage evidence.

project.status: Zapple-II / BP/M now includes a kernel-backed NETCCP remote-login server with Telnet option negotiation and terminal-independent command output; network execution remains upstream-reported.
techniques: CP/M Telnet and WGET client integration

identity.narrative: NETCCP remains part of the same Apple IIe/SoftCard Zapple-II and BP/M environment rather than a separate catalogue project.

classification.narrative: This is original CP/M-compatible system and networking development for legacy Apple II/SoftCard hardware, not reverse-engineered game code.

source_cpu.narrative: Original/inspected source architecture is 6502, Z80. This is not an inferred minimum runnable machine.

target_cpu.narrative: Inspected implementation/build establishes 6502, Z80 output architecture; a complete minimum runtime configuration was not independently verified.

build.narrative: The kernel-backed NETCCP server now negotiates Telnet ECHO/SGA, refuses client LINEMODE and receives cleanup plus terminal-independent output fixes.
build.limitations: The tracker did not run the server or repeat a remote-login session, so interoperability remains an upstream claim.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed server commits provide no new minimum Apple II, SoftCard, memory or W5100 firmware profile.

ai.narrative: Unknown: bounded primary documentation, sampled implementation/build/licence files and up to three latest full commit messages contain no explicit AI-contribution attribution. Absence is not evidence of non-use.

relationships.narrative: Screened against existing tracker projects and research decisions; no duplicate established.

project.status: Amiga Disk Engine now follows executable control flow into functions, cross-references and call graphs, names proven library calls, and exports source that GNU as rebuilds byte-for-byte across 39,363 corpus programs.

identity.narrative: The disassembly suite is a new capability within Amiga Disk Engine's existing disk/container/filesystem toolkit, not a separate project or game reconstruction.

classification.narrative: The project remains an original preservation and software-archaeology tool. Its new code-following disassembler is broadly reusable rather than a baked emulator for one title.

source_cpu.narrative: The reviewed inputs are disk structures, Workbench icon records and ILBM image data rather than one executable architecture.

target_cpu.narrative: The existing x86-64 host output evidence remains; the decoded-format work does not establish an additional host architecture.

build.narrative: Control-flow walks begin at loader entry points rather than linearly sweeping data, expose functions/xrefs/call graphs, name calls only after proving the library base, and export source rebuilt byte-for-byte with GNU as for all 39,363 corpus programs.
build.limitations: The tracker did not repeat the corpus run. Upstream explicitly leaves Devpac and vasm export compatibility untried.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The new disassembly/export feature states no additional host CPU, RAM or OS minimum.

ai.narrative: The reviewed feature commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5; this establishes an attributed contribution to this feature, not independent validation of its corpus results.

relationships.narrative: AROS icon.library and ilbm.datatype are documented behavioral references read locally and not copied into the repository; ADFlib remains a black-box differential oracle rather than a linked dependency.

project.status: amiga-re-kit 0.8.4 fixes long-run CIA timing, A500-style 24-bit/chip-RAM address decoding and CPU-versus-Copper register precedence from Alien Breed II full-game runs.

identity.narrative: Version 0.8.4 remains the same measured Amiga reverse-engineering and recompilation toolkit; Alien Breed II is a regression workload, not a separate bundled project record.

classification.narrative: This is original reverse-engineering/recompilation tooling whose runtime model is corrected from whole-game observations; it is not itself a recovered game source tree.

source_cpu.narrative: Architecture context: m68k. Source and target roles are recorded separately.

target_cpu.narrative: No minimum host instruction set established; a retro input platform is not a host CPU requirement.

build.narrative: Upstream full-game runs identified and fixed 32-bit wasm CIA timer exhaustion near 151,000 frames, A500 24-bit/chip-RAM mirroring and CPU/Copper register-write precedence that caused slowdown or a level-15 freeze.
build.limitations: The tracker did not run Alien Breed II or the web runtime, and the upstream observations do not establish compatibility with every Amiga title or configuration.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The commit models an A500 address bus for the recompilation runtime but states no minimum host CPU, RAM, browser or operating-system configuration.

ai.narrative: The 0.8.4 commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5; the attribution is scoped to the reviewed changes.

relationships.narrative: Related game projects are extraction provenance, not extra projects created from the toolkit directories.

project.status: PiST now analyzes TOS executables with persistent names/comments/code-data marks, live stopped-PC and Hatari coverage notes, picture inspection and source export admitted as a reconstruction only after vasm byte matching.

identity.narrative: The new TOS-program analysis tab is integrated into PiST's existing Atari ST IDE/debugger rather than a separate disassembler project.

classification.narrative: PiST remains a general Atari ST development and software-archaeology environment. It distinguishes guessed picture readings and only labels exported source a reconstruction after assembled bytes match.

source_cpu.narrative: PiST targets Atari ST/STE source projects written for Motorola 68000; this source architecture is retained independently of host package architectures.

target_cpu.narrative: v0.10.4 publishes Linux and Windows x86-64 packages plus macOS arm64 packages. These establish host outputs without implying minimum CPU generations.

build.narrative: The analysis module reads TOS programs, persists names/comments/forced code-data ranges, follows the live basepage and stopped PC, imports executed-address coverage, shows selected spans as pictures and checks source export with vasm.
build.limitations: The tracker did not run PiST, Hatari or vasm; the result is capability evidence, not proof that arbitrary binaries are correctly recovered.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Existing v0.10.4 Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64 and macOS arm64 profiles remain current; the analysis commits add no new CPU, RAM or OS minimum.

ai.narrative: The reviewed v0.10.4 release notes provide no explicit development-AI attribution; configuration files are not treated as proof of contribution.

relationships.narrative: PiST pins its Hatari fork to commit 41fc91d and rejects a built binary lacking the required coverage command. The fork is an explicit integrated dependency, not promoted as a second project by this pass.

project.status: DCTelnet now builds with m68k-amigaos GCC 16.2, and its GCC binary restores cursor-key navigation in the shell and Mystic BBS by correcting signed CSI-byte handling.

identity.narrative: DCTelnet remains the maintained Amiga Telnet/BBS client derived from the published 1.5/1.6 sources.

classification.narrative: The new commits are source maintenance and compiler-portability work, not binary reconstruction or a new terminal project.

source_cpu.narrative: README explicitly says the original 1.5/1.6 releases were compiled for 68020+; this source-maintenance lineage is distinguished from the new 68000 output.

target_cpu.narrative: src/Makefile explicitly builds separate 68000 and 68020 variants using VBCC or GCC.

build.narrative: Upstream enables m68k-amigaos GCC 16.2 and reports a working GCC binary after changing CSI from a signed character constant to numeric 0x9B; cursor keys then work in the shell and Mystic BBS reader as they did in the VBCC binary.
build.limitations: The tracker did not compile or run either binary. Runnable and compilable flags reflect the upstream build and exercised-binary report, not independent verification.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The existing AmigaOS 2.0+, 68000 minimum profile remains supported; GCC 16.2 changes the toolchain rather than the documented runtime floor.

ai.narrative: Earlier current-line maintenance explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5, including the ibmcon screen-buffer and blink feature. The attribution does not imply that every DCTelnet change used AI.

relationships.narrative: Credits Zed's Aminet sources, Bruno Frederic and spotUP improvements, and third-party ReqTools/XPR/XEM sources. LICENSE states original code remains all rights reserved. The repository URL and title were compared with the current catalogue; no equivalent project record was found.
